title: Toward XRF-like chemical sensitivity in the laboratory: first hyperspectral x-ray imaging demonstration using the novel CITIUS detector
task: Demonstrating hyperspectral X-ray imaging with novel CITIUS detector for laboratory-based chemical sensitivity
key_results: Sharp energy resolution 0.5–0.8 keV (FWHM) achieved; element-sensitive imaging separates materials with similar attenuation (water vs. polypropylene); approaches XRF-like chemical sensitivity without synchrotron
comments: CITIUS detector with liquid MetalJet source elegantly bypasses inefficiency of focused-beam XRF, enabling practical lab-scale hyperspectral tomography.

model_io.model: Hyperspectral X-ray micro-CT with CITIUS detector

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hyperspectral detector combined with MR-BMD enables XRF-like chemical sensitivity in laboratory setting
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: accurate material identification and quantification with sub-keV resolution

title: A flexible Bayesian framework for atomic masses by locally inferring configuration mixing
task: Developing probabilistic nuclear mass model with configuration mixing
key_results: SPICE model achieves ~500 keV root-mean-square deviation using 10-13 parameters; local Bayesian averaging captures evolving shell structure in neutron- and proton-rich regions
comments: Bayesian uncertainty quantification is rigorous, but extension to non-orthogonal configurations remains theoretical.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Local configuration mixing improves mass predictions beyond standard shell models
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: sub-500 keV accuracy with reduced parameters, insights into shell evolution

title: Sustainability as a challenge in complex systems dynamics
task: Analyzing emergent collective dynamics in infrastructure systems for sustainable development
key_results: Identification of flow disruptions, supply fluctuations, and non-equilibrium states in electric energy and sustainable mobility systems
comments: Review emphasizes multidisciplinary integration but lacks quantitative metrics or predictive models for failure prevention.
